question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

headers.www-authenticate: Bearer realm="OAuth", error="invalid_token", error_description="Missing or invalid access token"

decoded.protected-resource-metadata: none found: the challenge names no resource_metadata; GET https://mcp.intercom.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp (the RFC 9728 path for the resource) answers 404 text/plain, and so does the origin-level https://mcp.intercom.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (checked by hand at 18:16Z, transcript extra-well-known-1816Z.txt beside the artifact)
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.intercom.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (found by hand at the origin, since no protected-resource document names it): issuer https://mcp.intercom.com; registration_endpoint present (/register); PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, refresh_token; token auth client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none; no scopes_supported key
decoded.rest: GET https://api.intercom.io/me with no Authorization header answers 401 with www-authenticate Basic realm="intercom.io" and code missing_authorization; a Cloudflare bot-management cookie set by the MCP host is redacted in the transcript

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.intercom.com/mcp answers 401 with a Bearer challenge (realm OAuth, error invalid_token, a description) that names no resource_metadata, and the same error as JSON. No protected-resource metadata exists at either RFC 9728 path: the resource-specific one and the origin-level one both answer 404, so the discovery chain RFC 9728 describes stops at the first step. The server does publish authorization-server metadata at its origin, which is where the older MCP authorization convention looks: dynamic registration, PKCE S256, two grants, public and confidential clients, and no scope list. The current MCP authorization specification (2025-06-18) requires servers to publish that document and clients to read it; the 2025-03-26 revision looked for the server document at the resource's origin, which is where Intercom's is. A keyless GET on the REST API answers 401 with a Basic challenge, not Bearer. Same challenge shape as the 2026-09-12 measurement in the entry's notes; the absent resource document is recorded here for the first time. Nothing here measures what either server does with a credential.
